activities.label: Product rule model
activities.title: Product rule pattern
activities.body: Review the model and the example carefully. Then move on to your own explanation.

essentialIdeas: Use the product rule when differentiating a product of two functions: take the derivative of the first times the second, plus the first times the derivative of the second.

activities.label: Explain product rule
activities.title: Say the product rule
activities.body: Answer from memory in your own words. Keep it short and concrete.
activities.concept: Product rule
activities.correctAnswer: To differentiate a product of two functions, differentiate the first and multiply by the second, then add the first times the derivative of the second.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names both terms and makes clear that both functions stay in the expression. If needed, repair the missing plus sign or the idea that only one factor gets differentiated.

activities.label: Fix the product rule
activities.title: Repair the product rule
activities.body: Correct the missed step in one sentence, then rewrite the rule once.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Differentiating a product means differentiating only one factor and leaving the other unchanged.
activities.concept: Product rule
activities.correctAnswer: Differentiate both factors in a split way: first derivative times second, plus first times second derivative.
activities.feedback: The fix is to keep both original factors and add the two terms. If your first attempt left out one term, restore the missing plus term before moving on.

activities.label: Chain rule model
activities.title: Chain rule pattern
activities.body: Review the model and the example carefully. Then move on to your own explanation.

essentialIdeas: Use the chain rule for a composite function: differentiate the outer function, then multiply by the derivative of the inner function.

activities.label: Explain chain rule
activities.title: Say the chain rule
activities.body: Answer from memory in your own words. Use the same kind of short explanation.
activities.concept: Chain rule
activities.correctAnswer: For a composite function, differentiate the outside rule first, then multiply by the derivative of the inside function.
activities.feedback: A complete answer connects the outside and inside parts. If needed, repair the missing idea that the inside derivative multiplies the outside derivative.

activities.label: Choose the chain rule
activities.title: Pick the composite rule
activities.body: Choose the rule that fits this situation.
activities.concept: Chain rule
choices: Differentiate the outside function, then multiply by the derivative of the inside function.
Differentiate each part separately and add the results.
Differentiate only the inside function and leave the outside unchanged.
Differentiate only the outside function and ignore the inside.
activities.correctAnswer: Differentiate the outside function, then multiply by the derivative of the inside function.
activities.feedback: This is the chain rule for a composite function. The key is that the inner derivative multiplies the outer derivative.
